found: caps.enumerate_caps for wire C inside the planes C = 31 (scatter_table.py 28 31, state 27), then the one-cell rake of wire C sent at each cap
note: Wire C (stators (0,1,2), (0,1,4); sites (1,0,0), (1,0,2), (0,2,3)) between two caps; capL is the image of capR, one generation on, under the mirror (x,y,z) -> (z-4, y, x+4). One extra cell (1,0,4) in a unit of wire C is a rake: it runs towards +v at one unit per 2 generations and sends a 2-cell pulse back every 4 generations. capR turns the rake round (it comes back as its mirror image, which sends its pulses the other way) and swallows the pulses; so does capL. The rake shuttles for ever: period 4N + 2 for N units of wire.
